text.p: Telecommunications companies WorldCom Inc. and MFS Communications Inc. have completed their $12.6 billion stock swap merger, WorldCom announced Tuesday.
The combined companies, which will do business under the WorldCom name, will offer local, long-distance and international phone service and Internet services, the Jackson, Miss.-based company said.
Each share of MFS will be converted into the right to receive 2.1 shares of WorldCom common stock, WorldCom said. Preferred shares of MFS will be converted into preferred shares of WorldCom.
Before the merger, Omaha, Neb.-based MFS provided local calling service to businesses, while WorldCom was a long-distance and international carrier.
In August, MFS acquired UUNET, a major provider of Internet services, for $2 billion. The merger with WorldCom was announced later that month.
Cost savings between the two companies will be achieved from reduced line and access costs and the elimination of duplicate capital spending, WorldCom said.
The deal, however, is expected to hurt the combined companies' per-share earnings for three years, WorldCom said.
